label: test-silently-skips-or-cannot-fail
name: A test exists but does not run, or cannot fail on the defect it claims to guard: hidden tag, bare return, hardware-probe gate, fake that discards output, stale artifacts
description: What breaks: the only independent formula check of the packed-V layout sits after the available() early return so it skips on CI hosts without AMX (4188336256); a bare `return;` above the REQUIREs (2737861302 'did you intend to leave this return?'); a Catch2 tag changed to '[.name]' hides the test by default (2790161683 'did you intend to disable this test?'); pos_fake::xfer_n_blocks discards every descriptor argument so wrong HBM bases, fetchers, offsets or lengths pass (3960538177); a replay test writes /tmp/*.json and for_agent/*.json and reads the same pattern back with no cleanup, so a stale file can pass as a current result (2737978696). Procedure (check 3 widened): for each new or changed assertion list every exit, hidden tag, stub or build gate between the TEST_CASE start and the assertion; for every fake on the call path check whether its method bodies use the parameters the production code emits; list ofstream/fopen paths and check for delete-or-unique-name before the read-back; ask which production break makes the assertion fail on the gating lane.
disposition_reason: Check 3's trigger is a hardware probe before a formula assertion; the corpus shows four more ways the same test never observes the defect (hidden tag, bare return, parameter-discarding fake, stale artifact). The trigger must widen.
agent_feasibility: yes: Catch2 tags starting with '.', unconditional return above REQUIRE, fake methods with unused parameters, file writes without cleanup; the hardware gate still needs the runner table.

members.concern: The only check of the packed-V layout against an independent hand-written formula sits after the `available()` (AMX hardware probe) early return, so it silently skips on CI hosts without AMX; the other section does not cover it because at() and append_v_row share the same address helper (pair_base); move it above the return or into t_llama_unit.

detection.trigger: A test adds a runtime assertion comparing stored bytes/indices with a literal table or formula written in the test, and above it in the same TEST_CASE stands a return/SKIP conditioned on a hardware or environment probe (available(), cpuinfo flag, FPGA presence, getenv).
detection.procedure: read the full test file at HEAD and record every early exit between the TEST_CASE start and the assertion (here `if (!available()) return;` at line 197); find the oracle of the assertion; for every other assertion on the same storage (the at() section in t_llama_unit) check whether its expected side goes through the same production helper as the actual side (grep pair_base in v_vnni.hpp and in both call paths); record which CI lane compiles the target and whether its runners pass the probe (README.ci.md runner table).
detection.question: If the address formula were wrong, which assertion fails on the lane that gates the PR, on a runner without the hardware?

members.quote: This is the only check of the packed layout against an independent formula, but it sits after the `available()` early return (line 197), so it silently skips on hosts without AMX. The `at()` section in t_llama_unit doesn't cover it: `at()` and `append_v_row` share `pair_base`

Facts relied on: the early return 30 lines above the hunk; the shared helper pair_base in h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp used by both at() and append_v_row; CI runners have no AMX. Author moved the byte comparison into t_llama_unit as case 'append_v_row matches the independent packed-V formula' tagged [kv_data].

members.concern: A bare `return;` was added right after the new save loop in TEST_CASE save_k_and_v_to_hardware, which skips every assertion below it; Wade asks whether that was intended.

detection.trigger: A test hunk adds an unconditional `return;`, `SKIP()`, `break`, or `#if 0` inside a TEST_CASE/SECTION body above existing REQUIRE/CHECK lines.
detection.procedure: For each added early exit in t/, count the REQUIRE/CHECK lines between it and the end of the TEST_CASE at HEAD; if the count is greater than zero and no comment explains the exit, flag it as a disabled test.
detection.question: Does any assertion sit below this exit, and is the exit deliberate and documented?

members.quote: did you intend to leave this `return`?

Wade approved at 2d53016b44 before the removal was confirmed in the digest (comment at commit 620d1e83ba; final head is later, so the removal may be in the final head).

members.concern: The test tag of 'save_k_and_v_to_hardware' changed from '[save_k_and_v_to_hardware]' to '[.save_k_and_v_to_hardware]'; in Catch2 (the C++ test framework) a tag starting with '.' hides the test from the default run, so the PR silently disables the test. Wade asks whether that was intended.

detection.trigger: A diff line inside a TEST_CASE or TEST_CASE_METHOD macro changes a tag to begin with '.' (Catch2 hidden tag), adds '[!mayfail]' or '[.]', wraps a test in '#if 0', comments out a REQUIRE, or removes a test from t/CMakeLists.txt, and no PR body or commit sentence says the test is being disabled.
detection.procedure: grep the diff for '^\+.*TEST_CASE.*"\[\.' and for '^-.*REQUIRE\|^-.*CHECK' and for removed add_test lines. For each hit grep the PR body and commit subjects for the test name or 'disable'. If absent, ask whether it is intended. Also compare with pre-existing hidden tags in the same file (here stream_k_and_v was already '[.stream_k_and_v]') to tell a typo from a pattern.
detection.question: Does this hunk stop a test from running by default, and does any PR text state that this is intended?

members.quote: did you intend to disable this test?
members.note: The author's next commit d4795f37a5 'reenable test I typoed' restored the tag; at head line 500 reads '[save_k_and_v_to_hardware]'. Wade approved two minutes after that push. Check 3 covers tests that do not execute on the gating lane because of runtime hardware probes; a hidden Catch2 tag is a selection gate that check 3 only mentions in passing ('a separate gate; list them under selection'), hence partial.

members.concern: The new batch tests cannot detect wrong DMA destinations because the fake device's xfer_n_blocks (src/pos/fake.cpp) discards every descriptor argument; the tests check staging bytes and descriptor counts only, both start at GOF index zero, so wrong HBM bases, fetchers, source offsets or lengths would pass; Wade asks for an existing CI suite to capture descriptors at the transfer boundary and compare coalesced versus singleton transfers, with nonzero indices, partial windows and page-boundary runs.

detection.trigger: A new test asserts on a count, a size or a sample of intermediate values (descriptor_count, batch->size, selected staging entries) while the production call under test hands its real output (descriptors, addresses, lengths) to a fake or stub that ignores them; and every new case uses the zero/first index.
detection.procedure: Read the test's REQUIRE/CHECK lines and list what they observe. Follow the call under test (shard::xfer_gofs) to the device entry point (xfer_n_blocks) and read the fake implementation in src/pos/fake.cpp: do the arguments reach any storage a test can read? Enumerate inputs the tests vary (GOF indices, window fullness, page boundary) and list which equivalence classes are absent. Ask what a plausible bug (off-by-one base, wrong fetcher, wrong length) would change in the observed values.
detection.question: If the production code emitted the wrong destination address, fetcher, offset or length, which assertion in the new tests would fail?

members.quote: `pos_fake::xfer_n_blocks` (`src/pos/fake.cpp:336–346`) discards every descriptor argument. These tests inspect selected staging values and descriptor counts, so incorrect HBM bases, fetchers, source offsets, or transfer lengths would still pass.
members.note: Fit with check 3 is partial: check 3's theme is 'the assertion that would catch the bug never executes'; here the assertion executes but observes a quantity the bug does not change, with the fake as the sink. Wade's finding shape: bold 'Coverage gap:' headline, the mechanism fact with file:line, the equivalence-class list the tests lack (nonzero index, partial window, page boundary), the ask 'extend an existing CI suite' (not a new file), and a closing 'the current packing assertions do not establish that contract'. He also asks for a differential oracle (coalesced == singleton bytes at the same HBM locations). Head 7f80aa17da evidence: fake.cpp:376-390 xfer_n_blocks now records {dev->idx, bases[i], fetchers[i], ...} into fake_dma_captured_transfers under fake_dma_capture_enabled; t_phase1_integration.cpp:790 fake_dma_capture_guard, :1024 'partial odd-head GOF run keeps fixed K and V strides'.

members.concern: The new replay test writes dump files (/tmp/*.json and for_agent/hw_output_iter*.json) and reads back *_k/_v/_q/_hw/_sw.json; Wade asks whether each run deletes the artifacts of the previous run so stale files cannot be read back as current results.

detection.trigger: A test file adds std::ofstream / fopen / fs::create_directories or hard-coded output paths (/tmp/..., a relative directory) and also reads files by the same pattern.
detection.procedure: grep -n 'ofstream\|fopen\|/tmp/\|\.json"' t/<file>; grep -n 'remove\|unlink\|remove_all\|temp_directory_path' t/<file>; if writes exist and no removal, flag; also check whether the read side can pick up a file from an earlier run (same fixed name).
detection.question: Does the test delete or uniquely name the files it writes, so a rerun cannot read a stale artifact?

members.quote: does this test clean up any existing artifacts it previously generated, each time it runs?
members.note: At head 2d53016b44 t_hwattention_replay.cpp writes /tmp/k_cache_round_trip_dump.json (:124), /tmp/v_cache_round_trip_dump.json (:229) and for_agent/hw_output_iter{:02}.json (:582-583); grep for remove/unlink/filesystem:: finds nothing, so no cleanup exists. Comment anchored at line 1 (file-level), no reply, approved 34 minutes later.

codex_bullets.bullet: Check the oracle. Two accessors sharing the same address helper can agree while both are wrong. A fake that drops transfer arguments cannot prove correct destinations or lengths.
codex_bullets.reason: Three comments (PRs 4557, 4128, asim 244). The fake-boundary half (what arguments the fake records or discards) is new to the Claude skill.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: partial (check 3 covers the shared helper; the fake boundary has no check)

codex_bullets.bullet: Choose boundary cases from the failure mechanism: nonzero offsets, partial windows, page boundaries, queue wrap and full states, competing producers, branch fanout, and unsupported shapes. Do not add a generic matrix unrelated to the change.
codex_bullets.reason: Four Wade comments (PRs 4128, 2903) plus Wade's own closing line after the 2233 paste. Claude check 4 is about duplicates, not about which boundary cases to add.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: partial (check 4 says "prefer small cases"; no boundary list)

codex_bullets.reason: Four Wade comments (PRs 4557, 2698, 2011, 1920) plus the 3879 paste. Claude check 3 already states the four facts.
